subject.title: feat(hooks): emit session prune lifecycle event

question: Should session:prune expose toolNames and await internal hook handlers, or should the event be counts-only and non-blocking/time-bounded before merge?
rationale: This PR creates a new internal hook contract in a context-building path; automation cannot safely choose the permanent metadata and availability boundary for hook consumers.

options.title: Require safe non-blocking hook semantics
options.body: Port the hook to the active path, make delivery non-hanging or time-bounded, and expose only documented safe metadata before merge.

options.title: Accept awaited raw metadata as internal contract
options.body: Maintainers can explicitly decide internal hooks may receive raw toolNames and may delay pruning, but that should be a conscious compatibility/security choice.

options.title: Pause in favor of design issue
options.body: Keep the linked feature request as the canonical design item if this stale branch is no longer the right implementation vehicle.

recommendation.title: Require safe non-blocking hook semantics
recommendation.body: Port the hook to the active path, make delivery non-hanging or time-bounded, and expose only documented safe metadata before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans the internal hook system, active context-pruning path, and hook security/availability contract where history shows prior ownership.
